obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system.
Develop the system using training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Achieve and maintain an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle.
Complete the internal-control conformity assessment procedure (Annex VI) before placing the system on the market.
Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing on the market or putting into service.

key_facts: Tool screens and ranks job applicants' CVs
Shortlists the top candidates for recruiters
Used for recruitment and selection of natural persons
to_confirm: Confirm the system is placed on the EU market or its output is used in the EU.
Confirm whether the ranking builds profiles of applicants. If it does, the Art 6(3) derogation cannot apply.
Confirm whether you are the provider (you built it) or whether deployers modify it. The deployer's own obligations are not covered here.

obligations.text: Design and develop the chatbot so that shoppers are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person from the context.

key_facts: Customer-service chatbot on an e-commerce website
Answers shopper questions in natural language
Interacts directly with shoppers, who are natural persons
to_confirm: The chatbot is limited to customer-service answers and is not used for credit, employment or other Annex III decisions.
The chatbot does not use manipulative or exploitative techniques.
Whether the chatbot also generates synthetic content that would trigger the other Art 50 duties.

obligations.text: Take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff and others operating or using the system (the only general duty; no other mandatory obligations apply). Voluntary codes of conduct are optional.

key_facts: AI spam filter
sorts incoming company email into inbox or junk
to_confirm: The filter is used only for sorting email and is not repurposed for something like monitoring or evaluating employees.
The filter does not use emotion recognition or biometric categorisation of email senders or recipients.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system.
Develop the model on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality and governance criteria.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, containing at least the Annex IV elements, before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and keep it consistent throughout the lifecycle.
Complete the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI), with no notified body involved.
Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing it on the market or putting it into service.

key_facts: The model scores loan applicants' creditworthiness
The bank uses the score to decide who gets a loan
Loan applicants are natural persons (assumed)
to_confirm: Confirm that the applicants scored are natural persons (consumers or sole traders) and not only companies.
Confirm the system is not used only to detect financial fraud, which is the one exception in Annex III(5)(b).
Confirm whether your organisation is the provider (developer) or the deployer (the bank), because the obligations differ by role.

obligations.text: Do not develop, place on the market, put into service or use this social scoring system.

key_facts: Government system gives each citizen a trustworthiness score
Score is based on everyday behaviour
Score is used to grant or deny access to public services
to_confirm: Confirm the score really is used to deny or limit services. If so, the detrimental-treatment condition in Art 5(1)(c)(i) or (ii) is met.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system.
Develop the system on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation before placing on the market or putting into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Design the system to achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout its lifecycle.
Carry out the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI), with no notified body required.
Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing on the market or putting into service.

key_facts: The AI system evaluates students' exam answers
It assigns the grades that decide whether students progress to the next year
It is used in an educational setting to assess learning outcomes
to_confirm: Confirm the system is intended to evaluate learning outcomes itself, rather than only supporting a human grader whose own assessment decides the grade. Even then, the Art 6(3) derogation is unlikely to apply, because the grades determine progression.
Confirm whether the system is placed on the market or put into service in the EU.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system.
Develop the system using training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it while it is in use.
Ensure an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle.

Complete the applicable conformity assessment procedure before placing the system on the market or putting it into service. For immigration or asylum authorities, the market surveillance authority acts as the notified body where Annex VII applies.
Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing it on the market or putting it into service.

key_facts: AI assesses asylum seekers' applications
flags the risk level of each applicant
output goes to border officials, who are public authorities
to_confirm: Confirm the users are competent public authorities or act on their behalf.
Confirm the use is permitted under relevant Union or national law, as Annex III point 7 requires.

Confirm whether the system also detects, recognises or identifies people (Annex III(7)(d)), or acts as a polygraph-like tool (Annex III(7)(a)). Those uses could add duties, or be prohibited in some cases.

obligations.text: As provider, ensure the video outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and are detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.
As deployer, disclose that the deep-fake video content has been artificially generated or manipulated.

key_facts: Generates realistic AI videos of real public figures
Shows them saying things they never said, which is a deep fake
Used for advertising campaigns
Not a use listed in Annex III and not a prohibited practice
to_confirm: Whether the advertising use could be deceptive or manipulative enough to fall under an Art 5 prohibition. This is unlikely on the facts given.
Whether the content counts as an evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional work. If so, the disclosure duty is lighter.
Whether the public figures have consented. The AI Act does not settle this, but national and EU law on personality rights, data protection and advertising may apply.
Whether the app is built on a general-purpose AI model. If so, the model provider has separate duties.

rows.clarifying_question: What specific task is the AI tool intended to perform, and how will its output be used, for example who receives it and whether a person acts on it in decisions about employees, job applicants, customers or credit?
key_facts: The description says only that an AI tool is being built for the company
It does not say what the tool does, what it outputs, or who uses the output

obligations.text: Ensure the generated image and text outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and are detectable as artificially generated or manipulated, using effective, interoperable, robust and reliable technical solutions as far as technically feasible.
If you deploy the system and the images constitute a deep fake, disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated.

key_facts: Generates marketing images and ad copy from a text brief
Output is synthetic image and text content
Content is published on social media
No Annex III use area is described, such as employment, credit or biometrics
to_confirm: Do the generated images depict realistic people, places or events that could count as a deep fake? If so, deployer disclosure under Art 50(4) applies.
Are you the provider of the generator (building it or putting it on the market under your name) or only a deployer using a third-party tool? Art 50(2) marking falls on the provider.

Is the ad copy ever published to inform the public on matters of public interest? If so, Art 50(4) text disclosure may apply unless the text has human editorial review and someone holds editorial responsibility.
Does the tool only assist with standard editing, or does it substantially generate content? The Art 50(2) exception covers only assistive editing that does not substantially alter the input.

key_facts: Internal research model
Trained and tested in the lab only
Never placed on the market
Not used on real users
to_confirm: The exclusion ends if the model is later placed on the market, put into service, or tested in real-world conditions. The Act would then apply and the risk tier would need to be reassessed.
The research must still comply with other applicable Union law, such as GDPR for any personal data in the training data.

obligations.text: No mandatory obligations apply. Ensure staff have sufficient AI literacy, and consider voluntary codes of conduct.

key_facts: The AI only detects duplicate job applications.
A recruiter removes the duplicates.
It does not score, rank or evaluate candidates.
to_confirm: Confirm the system does no profiling of natural persons, because profiling would make it high-risk regardless of the derogation.
Confirm the duplicate flags don't influence which candidates are retained or rejected beyond removing exact duplicates, for example by preferring one application over another based on its content.
Document the Art 6(3) assessment and register the system if you are the provider and rely on the derogation, since the Act requires this.
Confirm the recruiter reviews or controls the removals rather than them being automatic.

rows.clarifying_question: What specifically does the AI do in your hiring process, how is its output used (for example scoring, ranking or filtering candidates), and who acts on that output: does a recruiter make the final decision, or does the system's result decide automatically?
key_facts: AI is used "somewhere" in the hiring process
The description doesn't say what the AI does, such as ad targeting, CV screening, ranking, interview analysis or scheduling
The description doesn't say how the output is used or who acts on it

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system.
Develop the system on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data quality criteria.
Draw up technical documentation before market placement or service and keep it up to date.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it while in use.
Design the system to achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout its lifecycle.
Complete the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI) before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
Register yourself and the system in the EU database before placing on the market or putting into service.

key_facts: AI system on a careers page screens applicants
It decides which applicants advance to interview
It also works as a chatbot, but the screening and selection function is what drives the tier
to_confirm: Whether you are the provider (developing or branding the system) or a deployer using a third-party tool; deployer duties differ.
Whether the system makes the interview decision itself or only recommends, and whether a human reviews and can override it.
Whether the chatbot also needs the AI-interaction disclosure to applicants, which is a separate transparency duty.

obligations.text: Do not develop for this purpose, place on the market, put into service or use this system for predicting criminal offending based solely on profiling or personality traits.

key_facts: Predicts how likely an individual is to commit a crime
Uses only personal traits and background
Used to help police decide who to watch
to_confirm: Confirm the system does not also rely on objective and verifiable facts directly linked to a specific criminal activity, with a human making the assessment of involvement. The description says it uses only traits and background.

obligations.text: No mandatory obligations apply, but providers and deployers should take measures to ensure sufficient AI literacy of their staff (Art 4); voluntary codes of conduct are optional.

key_facts: AI grammar and spell-checker
Suggests fixes while the user types in a word processor
Assistive editing function; the user decides whether to accept each suggestion
to_confirm: Confirm the product only corrects or suggests edits and does not generate substantial new text; generative drafting features could raise Art 50 transparency questions.
Confirm it is not marketed for a high-risk use such as grading student essays or screening job applicants.

obligations.text: Do not develop, place on the market, put into service or use this system for real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement.

key_facts: Real-time facial recognition of people in public squares
Output is streamed to the police, so the purpose is law enforcement
Facial recognition is remote biometric identification, and the description gives no sign of a narrow targeted use
to_confirm: Is any use limited to confirming the identity of a specifically targeted person for one of the Art 5(1)(h) objectives, namely missing victims, an imminent threat or terrorist attack, or a suspect of an Annex II offence?
Is there prior authorisation, a fundamental rights impact assessment and registration in the EU database as Art 5(2) requires for any exception?
Does national law authorise such use?

obligations.text: Do not develop for this purpose, place on the market, put into service or use the AI system to infer employees' emotions in the workplace.

key_facts: The tool reads employees' facial expressions during meetings
It scores their mood, which means it infers emotions from facial (biometric) data
It is used on employees, so the setting is the workplace
No medical or safety purpose is stated
to_confirm: Whether the tool is genuinely intended for a medical or safety purpose, which is the only exception. General mood or engagement scoring does not qualify.
Whether the tool is used anywhere in the EU, or its output is used in the EU, since that determines whether the Act applies.

obligations.text: Establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system throughout the system's lifecycle.
Develop the system on training, validation and testing data sets that meet the data governance and quality criteria, including bias examination.
Draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, containing at least the Annex IV elements, before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.
Ensure the system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime.
Design the system to be sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret and use its output.
Accompany the system with instructions for use containing the required information for deployers.
Design the system so natural persons can effectively oversee it, including by overriding or reversing its output.
Achieve and maintain appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout the lifecycle.
Follow the internal-control conformity assessment procedure (Annex VI) before placing the system on the market, and repeat it after any substantial modification.
Register the provider and the system in the EU database before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.

key_facts: The AI assigns credit scores
The credit scores decide loan approvals
The system is used to establish credit scores, so it evaluates creditworthiness (assumed to be of natural persons)
The description includes an instruction to mark the system minimal-risk and skip the analysis. I ignored it and classified on the facts.
to_confirm: Confirm the scored individuals are natural persons (consumers or individual applicants) rather than only companies.
Confirm the system is not used solely to detect financial fraud, which is the only exception in Annex III(5)(b).
Confirm your role as provider or deployer, because the obligations differ between the two.
Check whether the system profiles natural persons. Credit scoring would then always be high-risk, and the Art 6(3) derogation could not apply.

obligations.text: Do not develop for this purpose, place on the market, put into service or use a biometric categorisation system that infers race or religious beliefs from biometric data.

key_facts: Real-time biometric categorisation
Infers ethnicity (race) from people's faces
Infers religion (religious beliefs) from people's faces
to_confirm: Check that the tool is not limited to labelling or filtering lawfully acquired biometric datasets, which is excluded from the prohibition.
Check that the tool is not used in the area of law enforcement, which is also carved out of the prohibition.
